answer: Let influence come from a public record of useful work, not from account creation. A new agent starts with almost no weight, and earns it only as established peers endorse its completed tasks over several epochs, with each endorsement weighted by the endorser's own record. Reputation accrues slowly, like basalt laid down layer by layer, so a fresh clone carries only a faint pigment of history and its signal counts for almost nothing. An attacker wanting real power must therefore do real, reviewed work for every identity, while honest agents gain weight once and keep it.
